reading: The first refusal of each probe. A refusal masks every later one, so each probe after the first removes what the one before it was refused for, and the map is the first refusal per operation with the earlier ones removed. The probes run in order: the notebook's call as it is; its tables named as the source names them; then without the relationships, the keys and the time columns passed in; then with the columns dropped from the data whose inference the core refuses, one rule at a time, until describe_source succeeds; then the notebook's schema made by editing what the core described (keys, relationships, the products' time column cleared, rowguid deleted) and materialized with inference_config, without it, with one hop, and without the text column, which reaches predict's result on both runners. What the probes removed is the scope this map gives T1.23 to T1.28a; a rule no probe reached past (predict with inference_config, a time column cleared in Schema.from_source) is not in it and stays refused (P1B). rust-host starts the core operations, so it has a probe only where the contract can carry the input (gaps). From T1.23 describe_source takes the tables as the notebook names them, its keys, time columns and relationships, passes over a timestamp for its values and chooses among several, so rust-host's probes from the notebook's own call on reach text_time (T1.25), python-core's from the relationships' removal on reach it too (the call with tables named has no core route until T1.24, whose bridge still refuses the relationships), and every probe once the text columns are dropped describes the source on both runners.
